predecessors.name: Lê dynasty
predecessors.text: Đàng Trong, the Lê court's south (Thuận Hóa, Quảng Nam and the coast to Phú Yên), without the Central Highlands (Kon Tum, Gia Lai, Đắk Lắk) and the Lâm Đồng and Đắk Nông edge cells

successors.name: Tây Sơn dynasty
successors.text: Gia Định and the Mekong delta, the last Nguyễn land, taken by the Tây Sơn in 1776-1777 (without Panduranga and the uplands)

successors.name: Nguyễn dynasty (Đại Nam)
successors.text: Gia Định, regained by Nguyễn Ánh

ledger.x: 1572: the Nguyễn lords stand as the south of the Lê court.
1600: the seat moves from Trà Bát to Dinh Cát (infobox 'Trà Bát (1570-1600)', 'Dinh Cát (1600-1626)'); Nguyễn Hoàng broke with the Trịnh-led court in 1600.
1611: the Nguyễn attack Panduranga.
1626: the seat moves to Phước Yên (infobox 'Dinh Cát (1600-1626)', 'Phước Yên (1626-1636)').
1636: the seat moves to Kim Long (infobox 'Kim Long (1636-1687)'); the page text puts the move to Phú Xuân in 1636, which the infobox does not.
1653: Kauthara falls.
1653: the Nguyễn annex Kauthara.
1653: the Nguyễn invade the north.
1656: the Nguyễn 'were pushed back to their original walls' and give up Hà Tĩnh; Cliopatria keeps them there until 1658.
1658: the Nguyễn first intervene in Cambodia.
1687: the seat returns to Phú Xuân (infobox 'Phú Xuân (1687-1712, 1738-1775)').
1692: Panduranga occupied.
1694: the Cham king is restored.
1695: Panduranga a Nguyễn client.
1698: the Nguyễn found Gia Định and Saigon.
1699: the delta contest is closed in the ledger.
1700: the Mekong delta passes under Nguyễn administration.
1712: the seat moves to Bác Vọng (infobox 'Bác Vọng (1712-1738)').
1715: the Siamese invade Cambodia against Nguyễn backing.

1717: 'In 1717, the Siamese king sent his army to invade Cambodia for the second time', 'Annam agreed by sending 50,000 troops'; 'The four Siamese armies that invaded Cambodia were all defeated', 'the remaining Siamese troops were withdrawn back to Ayutthaya' and 'The Siamese stopped the…
1738: the seat returns to Phú Xuân (infobox 'Phú Xuân (1687-1712, 1738-1775)').
1739: Cambodian counterattack on the coast.
About 1749: the fighting ends.
1755: a port on the Gulf of Siam.
1773: the Tây Sơn take Qui Nhơn.
15 November 1774: the Trịnh attack.
1775: the south-central coast from Quảng Nam to Khánh Hòa goes to the Tây Sơn.
1775: the court flees to Quảng Nam and then Gia Định (infobox 'Quảng Nam (1775)', 'Gia Định (1775-1777,...)').
1775: the Nguyễn lose Panduranga with the coast.
February 1775: the Trịnh take Huế.
1775: Thuận Hóa lost.
1776: the Tây Sơn take Gia Định.
1777: the contest ends with the lords' destruction.
1777: Gia Định and the delta pass to the Tây Sơn.
1778: Nguyễn Ánh retakes Gia Định.
1780: 'In 1780, in an attempt to strengthen his political status, Nguyễn Phúc Ánh proclaimed himself Nguyễn vương'.
1782: the Tây Sơn retake Gia Định.
1783: Gia Định changes hands again.

20 January 1785: the Siamese fleet called in by Ánh is destroyed ('the morning of 20 January 1785'), the Tây Sơn reach Gia Định in 1785, and 'Thepharirak and Nguyễn Ánh fled back to Bangkok'; Gia Long page: Ánh 'a refugee in Siam in 1785', there 'until August 1787'.
1785: the rump state ends.

wars.name: Nguyễn–Cham wars
wars.outcome: Nguyễn victory: Kauthara annexed in 1653; Panduranga occupied in 1692, restored in 1694 as King of Thuận Thành and a client state from 1695.

wars.name: Trịnh–Nguyễn War (first phase)
wars.outcome: Indecisive: the walls held; the Nguyễn invaded the north in 1653 and were pushed back by 1656; peace in 1673 with the Linh River as the border, for about a hundred years.

wars.name: Nguyễn campaigns in Cambodia
wars.outcome: Nguyễn gains: the Mekong delta under full Vietnamese administration by the end of the 17th century, a Gulf of Siam port secured in 1755.

wars.name: Siamese–Nguyễn struggle for Cambodia (1714-1717)
wars.outcome: Inconclusive: a Vietnamese army helped Ang Em in 1714; the Siamese invasions of 1715 and 1717 failed to take Battambang and were withdrawn, and Siam 'stopped the war and negotiated'; no border change is recorded.

wars.name: Taksin's war against the Nguyễn (1769)
wars.outcome: No territorial result recorded on the page: 'War was launched against the Nguyễn in 1769' under King Taksin.

wars.name: Tây Sơn rebellion against the Nguyễn
wars.outcome: Tây Sơn victory: Qui Nhơn captured in 1773, Gia Định in 1776; the Nguyễn lords destroyed by 1777 except Nguyễn Ánh, who fled to Siam.

wars.name: Trịnh–Nguyễn War (second phase)
wars.outcome: Trịnh and Tây Sơn victory: the Trịnh captured Phú Xuân in February 1775; the Nguyễn retreated to Quảng Nam and later to Gia Định.

certainty.note: The Cham frontier and the Khmer delta are approximate; the Central Highlands are not drawn (no page puts them under the Nguyễn); the northern wall near Đồng Hới is a fixed line but unsurveyed.

The northern border with the Trịnh is fixed by the 1673 peace (Gianh or Linh River) and is the one sharp line; the Cham, Cambodian and delta frontiers stay soft (the Gulf of Siam strip and Tây Ninh especially), so the era is soft.
